title: How did one ship stop world trade for six days?

post.caption: The World's Chokepoints: the Suez Canal, Part 1: the pharaohs' canals, Lesseps and the 1869 opening, the 1956 Suez Crisis, the Yellow Fleet and the Ever Given. Images: public domain (incl. NASA, Royal Navy). Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How did one ship stop world trade for six days?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In March 2021, the giant container ship Ever Given got stuck sideways in the Suez Canal, in Egypt.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Where exactly is the canal?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It cuts across Egypt, from Port Said on the Mediterranean to Suez on the Red Sea.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About a hundred and ninety-three kilometres of water, through the desert.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Why does it matter so much?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Without it, ships between Asia and Europe sail all the way around Africa. That's thousands of kilometres more.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Who dug it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Pharaohs and Persian kings dug early canals from the Nile to the Red Sea. The modern one was the dream of a French diplomat, Ferdinand de Lesseps.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Work began in 1859. Huge numbers of Egyptian peasants were forced to dig, many by hand. How many died is still debated.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It opened in November 1869, with a grand ceremony.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So Egypt got rich?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Not exactly. Egypt fell deep into debt, and in 1875 it sold its shares in the canal to Britain.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: When did Egypt take it back?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In July 1956, President Nasser nationalised it. Britain, France and Israel invaded. Under pressure from the United States and the Soviet Union, they pulled out.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The canal stayed Egyptian.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: After the 1967 war it closed for eight years. Fifteen ships were trapped in the Great Bitter Lake the whole time.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And the Ever Given?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It blocked the canal for six days. Estimates say billions of dollars of trade were held up every day.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Next time: the Red Sea's other gate, the Gate of Grief. Like the video and follow History Sketches.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments what you think!
